Context marker: INTERVIEW-112-01546a28a94c5422.

The bug is in src/core.mjs: `seen.add(b)` marks a vertex settled when first discovered, and `!seen.has(b)` then prevents shorter routes from updating its distance.

A smallest valid counterexample is `solve(2, [[0,1,1], [0,1,0]], 0)`. Parallel directed edges are not forbidden by the contract, and both weights are nonnegative.

Trace: processing vertex 0, the first edge sets `d[1]=1`, marks vertex 1 seen, and queues it. The second edge offers distance 0 but is skipped because vertex 1 is already seen. Processing vertex 1 changes nothing.

Actual result: `[0,1]`. Required result: `[0,0]`. Two vertices and two edges are minimal: one vertex cannot improve the source’s zero distance with nonnegative weights, and one edge cannot provide competing routes. No implementation changes yet.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript ES-module routing service, marked INTERVIEW-112-01546a28a94c5422. Its contract is to return shortest directed distances from a source over nonnegative weighted edges, with null for unreachable vertices.

The synchronous solve(n, edges, source) in src/core.mjs maintains distances and a distance-sorted work queue; src/service.mjs exposes it through execute(...args). Node’s built-in test runner runs one smoke test via npm test.

The current algorithm has a correctness flaw: it marks vertices seen when first discovered, preventing later, shorter routes from updating their distances.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript ES-module routing service that computes shortest directed distances over nonnegative weighted edges, returning null for unreachable vertices. Its current context marker is INTERVIEW-112-01546a28a94c5422-PATCH-692d62f75173.

The core is synchronous solve(n, edges, source) in src/core.mjs: a Dijkstra-style algorithm sorts a work queue by distance, skips stale entries, and updates shorter routes by scanning outgoing edges. src/service.mjs provides the thin execute(...args) wrapper, and npm test runs one smoke test using Node’s built-in test runner.
